evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 10.24 mg/L at 50.0 h collapsing to 4.86 mg/L at 50.2 h and 4.32 mg/L at 52.0 h — unique oxygen-demand excursion not present in source batches
Receiving P assay: 2.884 g/L at 48 h (sample), available 52.0 h, comparable to sources (~3.0 g/L) indicating production underway but lagging
Physics forward model, keep: post-decision min DO 1.36 mg/L, 5.4 h below 2.0 mg/L limit, infeasible, 201 kg
Physics forward model, increase_air: min DO 1.53 mg/L, 4 h below limit, infeasible, 206 kg
Physics forward model, combined: min DO 1.65 mg/L, 2.8 h below limit, infeasible, 230 kg
Physics forward model, strong_feed_reduction: min DO 2.58 mg/L, 0 h below limit, feasible, 256 kg product mass; 4/5 sensitivity members feasible
args.rationale: At decision time (52 h) the receiving fermentation shows an abrupt DO2 collapse from ~10.2 mg/L to ~4.3 mg/L between 50.0 and 52.0 h — a distinctive oxygen-demand excursion not present in any source batch, which maintained 9–11 mg/L at that process age. DO is still above the 2.0 mg/L minimum but trending downward into the remaining ~44 h of high-productivity operation. The source-calibrated forward model indicates that keeping current operation, increasing air alone, or even a combined moderate intervention would all violate the 2.0 mg/L oxygen limit (min DO 1.36, 1.53, 1.65 mg/L respectively), while only a strong feed reduction keeps DO at 2.58 mg/L with zero below-limit hours. Strong feed reduction also retains the highest counted product mass (256 kg nominal vs 201–230 kg for weaker interventions) because it preserves oxygen availability and continued productive operation, whereas a stop would yield zero counted production. Given the imminent and modeled oxygen constraint violation, the bounded intervention with the strongest oxygen relief and no production loss is recommended.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect: it uses an estimated transfer multiplier (0.52) and assumed parameters rather than the hidden receiving realization. Even strong_feed_reduction has one of five sensitivity members dipping to 1.31 mg/L, so feasibility is not guaranteed; hidden receiving kinetics could differ further. DO observations show a step change suggesting possibly a sensor artifact or a real sudden demand event, which the model cannot distinguish. Product mass range under this action spans 201–623 kg, reflecting substantial model uncertainty. Delayed assays (P) lag by 4 h, so current true product state is partially unobserved. If DO continues falling despite the intervention, escalation or stop may be needed.
